body.target_estimand: The primary binary estimand is \(\tau_N=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\{Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)\}=(p-q)/n\). For the bounded-class corollary, a schedule \(\mathbf y=(y_{i1},y_{i0})_{i=1}^n\in[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]^{2n}\) has causal ATE \(\tau(\mathbf y)=n^{-1}\sum_i(y_{i1}-y_{i0})\); on the binary endpoint embedding \(y_{id}=L_{\mathrm{bd}}+\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}Y_i(d)\), it satisfies \(\tau(\mathbf y)=\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}\tau_N\)
body.estimand_functional: The primary binary fixed-design functional is \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{CR}}=\min_t\max_{N\in\mathcal N_n}\sum_{x,y}K_N(x,y)\{t(x,y)-\tau_N\}^2\). The bounded-outcome corollary compares the fixed balanced-design functional \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{bal}}[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]\) with the all-design, all-measurable-estimator functional \(\mathfrak R_n^\star[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]\) from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}hull\mbox{-}bounded\mbox{-}minimax\mbox{-}risks}\)

sampling_model.design: Uniform assignment over \(\mathcal Z_n\), the assignments treating exactly \(m=n/2\) units.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) labeled units and both binary potential outcomes are fixed; the assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: One binary treatment with exactly \(m\) treated and \(m\) controls.
sampling_model.overlap: Every labeled exactly balanced assignment has probability \(1/\binom n m\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no stochastic nuisance estimation; nature ranges over the finite response-type state space \(\mathcal N_n\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Complete randomization is conjectured to remain strictly suboptimal for general estimators.
``For binary potential outcomes, we show this minimax risk is equivalent to the minimax risk of an estimation problem with \(2\) unknown parameters.''
``A new proof of this result is given, and the restriction to experiments with a finite number of outcomes is removed.''
``This paper shows the minimax optimality of the complete randomization scheme under permutation invariance.''

body.tldr: Exact balance removes treatment-share variation but leaves two observed arm-success counts. For fixed binary potential outcomes, the full pair and its difference have equal worst-schedule ATE squared-error minimax risk at \(n=2,4,6\), but a rational two-sided full-count bracket and a difference-only lower certificate prove strict loss at \(n=8\). The endpoint subclass also yields a separate bounded-outcome design result: balanced complete randomization is strictly worse than Hull's independent-design optimum at \(n=2,4,6,8\). Both later-even compression persistence and Hull's uniform-in-\(n\) strictness conjecture remain open.

project_justification.gap: Published minimax analyses establish the all-design shifted-binomial reduction and report numerical evidence that complete randomization remains strictly suboptimal with general estimators, but do not give exact endpoint certificates for that strict comparison. They also do not locate the first finite size at which compressing the two exact-balance success counts to their difference loses minimax information.
project_justification.niche: The fixed-half binary response-type hypergeometric experiment supplies exact primal-dual certificates, while its binary endpoint embedding supplies rigorous lower bounds for the full bounded schedule class without claiming a nonbinary two-count reduction.
project_justification.fill: The project gives analytic equality saddles at \(n=2,4,6\), rational lower and upper full-count certificates and strict count-compression separation at eight, and exact finite bounded-class comparisons showing balanced complete randomization is strictly suboptimal relative to independent assignment at \(n=2,4,6,8\).

body.related_work: Hull (2026, Theorem 1 and Appendix A.4) optimizes worst-case ATE squared error jointly over all bounded schedules, assignment designs, and measurable estimators, proves that independent half assignment attains the shifted-binomial minimax program, and uses Bernstein extension plus separate convexity to lift endpoint risks to the full bounded cube. Corollary 1 gives the affine independent-design risk \(\Delta^2/(\sqrt n+1)^2\); footnote 12 records uniform strict suboptimality of complete randomization with general estimators as a conjecture supported numerically. Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}hull\mbox{-}class\mbox{-}complete\mbox{-}randomization\mbox{-}strict\mbox{-}small\mbox{-}n}\) proves that comparison only for \(n=2,4,6,8\), leaving the uniform conjecture open. Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) study the same unrestricted independent-design scalar program and its Airy expansion, not the exact balanced hypergeometric count-compression threshold. Ding and Dasgupta (2016) supply the binary response types and observed table used in the finite kernel. Blackwell (1953) gives only weak dominance of the full count pair over its difference. Bai (2023) treats permutation-invariant linear procedures. Rigdon and Hudgens (2015), Li and Ding (2016), and Li and Ding (2017) concern exact confidence sets or first-order finite-population limits and do not imply the point-estimation or bounded-design claims here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The two rational full-count certificates at \(n=8\) are distinct: \(C_8<\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}<U_8\) is not proved, only \(C_8\leq\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}\leq U_8\), and \(C_8<U_8\), so the exact value remains unknown. An arbitrary prior can make the second count Bayes-informative even at sizes where the minimax values agree. The bounded-class result uses only the valid endpoint-subclass lower-bound direction and does not reduce nonbinary observations to two success counts.
body.honest_scope: The theorem-level scope consists of the exact binary response-type games, equality at \(n=2,4,6\), strict count-compression separation and a two-sided full-count bracket at \(n=8\), the resulting first-lossy-size conclusion, and strict bounded-class suboptimality of balanced complete randomization at \(n=2,4,6,8\). The paper makes no confidence-set claim, pointwise-dominance claim, exact \(\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}\) claim, or two-count orbit claim for nonbinary schedules. Strict count-compression persistence for even \(n\geq10\), Hull's uniform complete-randomization conjecture, and every asymptotic rate, exponent, parity law, or constant for the balance or compression tax remain open.
